paper_metadata.title: Quantum vs. Classical Machine Learning: A Benchmark Study for Financial Prediction

summary: The paper benchmarks quantum ML models for financial prediction across three tasks: directional classification (QNN vs ANN), live trading (QLSTM vs LSTM), and volatility forecasting (QSVR vs SVR/GARCH). QNNs slightly outperform ANNs on some assets (e.g., +3.8 AUC on AAPL and +4.9 AUC on KCHOL), QLSTM improves Sharpe ratio in 2 of 4 market regimes, and QSVR achieves the best QLIKE on KCHOL but generally trails classical RBF SVR. All experiments use small simulated circuits (≤10 qubits) without real quantum hardware.

experiments.description: Directional classification of next-day stock return direction using QNNs versus matched ANNs on Turkish equities, the S&P 500, and selected U.S. equities across low-, medium-, and high-dimensional feature regimes.

algorithm.variant: QNN family with four variants: QNN-SQ, QNN-MQ, Hybrid-SQ, Hybrid-MQ
algorithm.ansatz: parameterized rotation-gate ansatz with entangling operations (Rx, Ry, Rz; CZ entanglers for amplitude-encoded case)
algorithm.convergence_criteria: selected by highest mean validation AUC across 5 expanding-window folds

problem_formulation.encoding_method: angle_encoding (3-D and 7-D regimes) and amplitude_encoding (64-D regime)
problem_formulation.encoding_details: 3-D and 7-D feature sets use angle encoding with one qubit per feature; 64-D feature set uses amplitude encoding to reduce qubit count to 2-6 qubits
problem_formulation.objective_function: binary classification of next-day return direction (up/down)

problem_instance.description: Financial directional prediction on Turkish equities, S&P 500, and five U.S. equities using technical indicators, lagged returns, and cross-asset returns

dataset_specification.date_range: not fully specified; final fold test period 2020-01-02 to 2021-12-31
dataset_specification.preprocessing: min-max scaling; walk-forward expanding-window 5-fold CV; remove days with missing observations; adjusted close for individual equities, close for S&P 500
dataset_specification.train_test_split: 5-fold expanding-window cross-validation; results reported on final fold

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Technical indicators (RSI-14, %K14, 3-day SMA of %K14), lagged self-returns, and cross-asset lagged returns; min-max normalization fitted on training fold only; walk-forward expanding-window CV
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: 5-fold expanding-window cross-validation; model selected by mean validation AUC; final fold test results reported

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: min-max scaling; feature engineering from technical indicators and lagged returns

speedup_claims.conditions: Directional classification benchmark on Turkish equities, S&P 500, and selected U.S. equities; empirical comparison only
speedup_claims.caveats: No asymptotic or runtime speedup is reported; the paper only reports predictive performance differences.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Unknown; experiments use 3–7 qubits (angle encoding) or ≤6 qubits (amplitude encoding) with shallow circuits (≤6 layers) in statevector simulation.
limiting_factors: Results obtained only in noiseless simulation
Small qubit counts (≤7 angle or ≤6 amplitude)
ANN baselines outperform or match QNNs on most datasets
Feature encoding overhead dominates potential benefits

notes: Quantum models are simulated in TorchQuantum with statevector simulation and exact expectation values; no real QPU is used.
Qubit counts and depths are reported as search ranges and selected architectures across the three feature regimes.
No asymptotic quantum speedup is characterized; the paper is an empirical benchmark.
Tables IX–XI show QNNs sometimes slightly outperform ANNs (e.g., AAPL AUC improvement) but overall results are mixed with classical models often matching or exceeding performance.
Authors frame results as 'competitive' rather than demonstrating clear quantum advantage.

experiments.description: Live-trading simulation on the S&P 500 comparing QLSTM against classical LSTM across four market regimes with threshold-based trading signals and backtesting.

algorithm.variant: QLSTM based on Chen et al. with each LSTM gate replaced by a variational quantum circuit
algorithm.ansatz: variational quantum circuits inside LSTM gates
algorithm.convergence_criteria: early stopping when ES AUC fails to improve for 30 epochs; model selected by validation AUC; thresholds selected to maximize Sharpe

problem_formulation.encoding_details: 4 input features per day stacked into 10x4 windows; classical inputs are mapped into qubit rotations in each VQC block
problem_formulation.objective_function: predict next-day return direction and convert probabilities into long/short/neutral trading signals to maximize risk-adjusted return
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: threshold calibration on hold-out slice; transaction costs applied; no-trade region between thresholds

problem_instance.description: Return-based live trading on the S&P 500 across four regimes: Global Financial Crisis, Pre-Covid, Covid Shock & Recovery, and Post-pandemic

dataset_specification.preprocessing: adjusted-close prices; min-max scaling; 10-day rolling windows; expanding-window cross-validation with 4 folds
dataset_specification.train_test_split: each regime split 70/10/10/10 for train, early stop, model selection, threshold calibration

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Features are previous-day log return, MACD line, MACD signal, and RSI-14; all normalized to [0,1] using training-only scaler; rolling windows of length 10
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: 4 regime folds; early stopping on ES AUC; model selection by AUC; threshold calibration by Sharpe; final backtest on hold-out slice

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: min-max scaling; threshold calibration; backtesting with transaction costs
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: conversion of probabilities to trading positions using long/short thresholds

speedup_claims.conditions: Live-trading simulation on S&P 500 across four market regimes; empirical backtest only
speedup_claims.caveats: No computational speedup is claimed. Improvements are in risk-adjusted trading performance, not runtime.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: QLSTM circuits with 3–5 qubits and depth 2–6 inside each LSTM gate, simulated via statevector.
limiting_factors: Trading performance depends heavily on threshold calibration rather than inherent model advantage
QLSTM underperforms classical LSTM in one regime (post-pandemic)

notes: QLSTM is simulated in TorchQuantum; no real hardware device is named.
Qubit width and circuit depth are reported as search ranges for the QLSTM family.
No asymptotic speedup analysis is provided.
Table XII shows QLSTM outperforming LSTM in Sharpe ratio in two regimes but underperforming in another, indicating mixed outcomes.
Authors state QLSTM 'improves risk-adjusted returns in two of four regimes' but do not claim consistent superiority.

experiments.description: Volatility forecasting on S&P 500, AAPL, GARAN, and KCHOL using QSVR with angle encoding compared against classical SVR and GARCH.

algorithm.variant: QSVR with angle encoding / quantum kernel SVR
algorithm.ansatz: hardware-efficient RY-RZ rotations with ring of CZ entanglers
algorithm.convergence_criteria: best hyperparameters selected by Optuna; retrain on full in-sample window and predict one-step-ahead realized variance

problem_formulation.encoding_method: angle_encoding and amplitude_encoding (two separate QSVR feature-map variants)
problem_formulation.encoding_details: feature vector embedded into quantum state via repeated RY rotations and CZ entanglers; quantum kernel computed from statevector overlaps

problem_instance.description: Realized volatility forecasting for four equities using past returns and past realized variance

dataset_specification.preprocessing: standard scaling (z-score); expanding-window forecasting; initial training set 720 days; retrain every 120 days; total training window lengths tested at 1000, 2000, 3000, 4000 days

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Target is 5-day rolling realized variance; features are past returns and past realized variance; standard scaling; retraining schedule every 120 days
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: out-of-sample forecasting with QLIKE, MSE, R2, directional accuracy, and Diebold-Mariano tests

speedup_claims.conditions: Kernel evaluation for both classical and quantum methods
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper explicitly states both classical and quantum kernel evaluation scale as O(N^2); no speedup is shown.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Angle-encoded QSVR with ~10 qubits or amplitude-encoded QSVR with 5 qubits using shallow feature-map circuits (≤3 layers).
limiting_factors: RBF SVR consistently achieves best QLIKE values
Quantum kernel provides only intermediate performance
Experiments performed via exact statevector overlaps (not hardware)
Kernel matrix computation still scales O(N^2)

notes: QSVR is executed in simulation mode using TorchQuantum statevectors and exact overlaps; no real QPU is used.
The paper explicitly states kernel evaluation scales as O(N^2) for both classical and quantum kernels.
The reported qubit counts differ between angle-encoding experiments and are given in the results tables.
Tables XIII and XIV show classical RBF SVR generally achieving the best QLIKE scores across assets.
Paper explicitly states QSVRs fall between RBF SVR and linear/polynomial SVRs in performance.

experiments.description: Volatility forecasting with amplitude-encoded QSVR/QSVM variants at different feature dimensions, compared against classical SVR and GARCH.

algorithm.variant: Amplitude-encoded QSVR / QSVM with fixed post-unitary
algorithm.ansatz: random fixed unitary stack after amplitude encoding
algorithm.convergence_criteria: best hyperparameters selected by Optuna; retrain on full in-sample window and predict one-step-ahead realized variance
algorithm.parameter_initialization: randomly sampled unitary layer stack for the fixed post-unitary

problem_formulation.encoding_details: entire normalized feature vector embedded into state amplitudes; d=32 uses 5 qubits; paper also discusses d=16 and d=64 settings

problem_instance.description: Amplitude-encoded volatility forecasting on S&P 500, AAPL, GARAN, and KCHOL using lagged returns and realized variance

dataset_specification.preprocessing: standard scaling (z-score); expanding-window forecasting; initial training set 720 days; retrain every 120 days; total training window lengths tested at 1000, 2000, 3000, 4000 days

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Amplitude encoding applied to normalized feature vectors; paper notes performance degrades when dimension increases to 64
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: out-of-sample forecasting with QLIKE, MSE, R2, directional accuracy, and Diebold-Mariano tests

speedup_claims.conditions: Quantum and classical kernel evaluation in the same volatility forecasting pipeline
speedup_claims.caveats: No computational speedup is claimed; the paper emphasizes empirical forecasting comparison only.

notes: Amplitude-encoded QSVR/QSVM is simulated in TorchQuantum using exact statevectors; no real QPU is used.
The paper reports d=32 with 5 qubits in the amplitude-encoding table and discusses d=16, 32, and 64 behavior.
No asymptotic quantum advantage is claimed beyond empirical comparison.
